text:
anna: FYI we're getting steady p99 regressions on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 starting ~02:12 UTC. Not a single spike — sustained for ~45m.

josh: Seen it. p50 stable (~80ms) but p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~920ms. Error rate still low.

vivian: gpu-pool-eu-west-1-a queue length climbing, currently ~310 waiting requests per shard.

marc: Admission controller logs show a flood of 'max_batch_reached' and 'accepted_after_timeout'. Looks like requests are hitting the max_batch_size window and getting delayed.

anna: That matches traces — a lot of requests are small (tokens < 64) but arriving evenly so batches fill slowly and hit max_batch timeout. Continuous batching pressure, not sudden traffic spike.

sasha: infra-bot posted recent admission metrics:

```
// infra-bot summary
pool: gpu-pool-eu-west-1-a
rps: 1.6k
avg_batch_fill_time: 75ms -> 420ms
max_batch_size: 64
batch_timeout_ms: 100
deferred_by_qos: 8.4%
queue_depth: 312
p99_latency_tokens_only: 840ms
```

josh: The batch_timeout_ms (100ms) + slow fill is giving extra latency. Once batch waits, the scheduler has less headroom and downstream de-dup caches miss.

vivian: Also seeing many 'prefer_low_cost_variant' route overrides that push to the same GPU pool instead of fallback instances. Routing pressure concentrated in eu-west.

marc: Two options short term: lower max_batch_size to 48 or 32 to reduce fill time; OR increase parallel worker count (scale up workers on that pool). Which is lower risk?

anna: Lowering max_batch_size should reduce p99 but increases tokens-per-second costs slightly and may raise system throughput needs. Scaling workers requires capacity and may take ~10min to provision.

sasha: Can we try config flip on a single shard first? Canary to shard-3 in eu-west-1-a.

josh: +1. Patch admission config on shard-3: set max_batch_size=32, batch_timeout_ms=80. Monitor p99 and queue depth for 5m.

vivian: I'll roll the canary. Command:

```
# canary change
curl -X POST "https://controlplane/api/pools/gpu-pool-eu-west-1-a/shards/3/config"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRATOKEN"
  -d '{"max_batch_size":32, "batch_timeout_ms":80}'
```

infra-bot: config-update accepted for shard-3 (tx id: tx_0x7a2cd).

anna: After 90s, shard-3 p99 dropped from 910ms -> 230ms. queue_depth on shard-3 went 78 -> 22. Nice.

marc: Canary looks good. But overall pool p99 still ~700ms because other shards still saturated.

josh: Next step: either roll change to all shards (fast) or autoscale additional workers + bump capacity in infra (slower + cost). We should do config roll across pool now and autoscale in parallel.

vivian: Agree. I'll start rolling config to rest of shards with 30s stagger. Keep an eye on evictions and throughput.

sasha: Note cost note: moving max_batch_size 64->32 increases request throughput per GPU by ~18% (est), which may raise committed capacity costs if we hit utilization ceilings. But it's cheaper than SLA misses.

anna: Also added temporary routing change: prefer_low_cost_variant disabled for eu-west-1 for 20m to spread traffic.

infra-bot: routing override applied (scope: eu-west-1, ttl: 20m).

marc: After full roll (10m), pool p99 stabilized ~260-320ms and queue depth normalized ~30-60. We'll keep config for 2h then revert if throughput issues.

josh: Action items:
- vivian: complete pool-wide config roll (in progress)
- sasha: monitor cost delta, open quick PR if we need quota bumps
- anna: schedule autoscale policy tweak to add +2 workers per pool when avg_queue_depth > 150 for 5m
- marc: capture an incident note if p99 > 500ms after 2h

vivian: On it. Posting live metrics link: https://internal.metrics/redwood/eu-west-1/pools/gpu-pool-eu-west-1-a

anna: Thanks all. If we see reappearance after routing TTL, revert to previous and reopen more aggressive scaling. :eyes:

josh: thumbs up. Good quick mitigation — continuous batching pressure is subtle but repeatable.

sasha: filing follow-up doc on long-term fixes: adaptive max-batch sizing, request coalescing heuristics, and routing diversification.

infra-bot: note: incident_severity=low, sla_impact=partial_p99, start_ts=1839007654, mitigated_ts=1839007890

anna: Closing thread unless we see fresh regressions.
